events.description: Volunteer with NYC Parks for Trees Count 2025! At each event you will receive a tote bag with all the materials needed to count trees. Using our Tree Census app, you’ll split up into different zones within the park to start counting trees! After completing your first training event, you are welcome to continue counting trees on your own in smaller parks across the city. For your comfort and safety, please bring water and wear closed-toe shoes to this program.

events.title: Volunteer Day: Work + Learn at Hattie Carthan Herban Farm
events.description: GreenThumb community gardens are developed, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically maintain them as public green spaces.Hattie Carthan Herban Farm is hosting bi-weekly volunteer days to engage new volunteers and gardeners with the space! Join us for a hands-on Work and Learn Day at the Hattie Carthan Herban Farm! This recurring event includes around 2 hours of dedicated volunteer work, followed by a hands-on educational hour.Volunteer tasks include weeding, pruning, and mulching. Refreshments and all tools, including gloves, are provided.Harvest beneficial herbs, make a smudge stick, and more in a hands-on educational hour with Farmer Yon after the volunteer session! We meet every other Friday, 4 p.m.- 7 p.m.No prior experience necessary - beginners are welcome! GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.Register here! This is a great opportunity to support a dynamic community space while learning about urban agriculture. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Location: 49 Van Buren St, Brooklyn, NY 11221For information about group volunteering or questions about this event, contact Rain.Abdalla@parks.nyc.gov.This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Wheel Fun Rentals Celebrates America's 250th with Patriotic LED Bike Ride
events.description: Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. Families, couples, and friends can cruise along two of New York City's scenic waterfronts while celebrating America's historic 250th birthday.On July 4th, guests can make the holiday even more memorable by riding to waterfront viewing areas for spectacular fireworks displays. Launching from Bensonhurst Park in Brooklyn, riders can enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront bike path with views across New York Harbor. On Staten Island, guests can pedal along the FDR Boardwalk, where the waterfront provides a scenic setting to take in the evening's Independence Day celebrations and fireworks over the harbor.Night Rides are first-come, first-served and available Friday – Sundays and holidays beginning at sunset until 10pm, last 1-hour rental goes out at 9pm. Pricing is $29 for a Single Surrey (seats up to 3 adults and 2 small children), and $39 for a Double Surrey (seats up to 6 adults and 2 small children).For additional location information, current hours of operation, and to learn more about Wheel Fun Rentals available recreational rental options, visit wheelfunrentals.com/NYC.

events.title: Caribeando Community Music and Dance Workshop
events.description: Caribbean Music and Dance workshops with Juan Usera and the Sambuco Tribe in Van Cortlandt Park.Saturdays May, 9, June 6 and August 22 from 2-4pmFollowing their inspiring Caribeando performance at the Hostos Center for the Arts and Culture last May, Juan Usera and the Sambuco Tribe is offering an interactive Caribbean Music and Dance workshop in Van Cortlandt Park for the Bronx community.The Caribeando Community Music and Dance Workshop provides an excellent opportunity to learn and practice Caribbean musical and dance traditions rooted in African heritage. Participants will learn Bomba, Plena, Guaracha, Cha-cha-cha, Merengue, and more. All ages, abilities, and skill levels are welcome to explore the basic rhythms, steps, call-and-response interactions, and shared community joy.Workshop will be held next to the Enslaved African & Kingsbridge Burial Ground behind the Tennis Courts.Parking is available in the Van Cortlandt Golf Lot. No driving inside the park allowed.RSVP Now.This series is sponsored by The NYC Green Fund Grassroots Grant Program.This series is supported, in part, by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the New York City Council.

events.title: Community Work Day
events.description: Roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty at an upcoming volunteer day!Stop by the Wyckoff Urban Farm on the fourth Saturday of every month from April-October between 11AM-1PM to to volunteer alongside our farm staff to care for our space and participate in special work projects. Learn about what we're growing, get to know our farmers, and get your hands dirty with farm projects!Tickets are not required to attend, but it's always helpful to RSVP so we can plan projects accordingly.THINGS TO KNOW:This event is family-friendly (ages 10+). We welcome individuals and families with kids ages 10 and over but children must be accompanied by an adult for the duration of their stay.Dress for the mess! Make sure to wear clothes that you don't mind getting messy in and wear close toed shoes to protect your feet.Come Prepared: We will provide all the tools and protective gear for your projects but coming prepared with a hat, long sleeved shirt, sunscreen, and bug spray is always a good idea.Facilities: Water fountain and public restrooms are available on-site. We recommend bringing snacks and a refillable water bottle.Weather: Community Work Days are rain or shine. If extreme weather is expected, we will update this page and contact those on the RSVP list to cancel.Volunteer Groups: This event is intended for individuals, families, and small groups of 5 or fewer participants. Community organizations and corporate volunteer groups are welcome to make advance reservations by emailing info@wyckoffmuseum.org to discuss scheduling options and availability.
